implementation_notes: NServiceBus documents the invalid-message behaviour explicitly: when a message cannot be deserialized, all retry mechanisms are bypassed and the message is moved directly to the configured error queue, and validation failures can be declared unrecoverable with AddUnrecoverableException so they also skip retries. The handler therefore only has to validate semantic rules and throw; the framework owns the invalid channel, and moving the message is observable as an ERROR log entry that can drive alerting.
pitfalls: 'Unrecoverable' means never retried, so declaring a transient exception there sends recoverable messages straight to the error queue and hides outages.
Failed messages are copied to the error queue with the exception headers; without a retention or purge policy that queue quietly becomes a growing store of untrusted payloads.
The error queue name is a deployment convention - renaming or merging endpoints orphans previously failed messages.

variants.name: MassTransit *_error queue with the error pipe filters
variants.implementation_notes: MassTransit's default error pipe moves faulted messages to the *_error queue prefixed by the receive endpoint's queue name and stores the exception details as headers; the behaviour is customized per receive endpoint through ConfigureError, either by adding filters or by discarding faults when an external store owns them. The invalid channel is therefore the framework's error queue: the consumer validates and throws, the framework diverts, and Fault<T> events give observers a second, independent hook.
pitfalls: Discarding faulted messages (or binding an endpoint whose transport has no _error queue) turns the invalid channel into exactly the black hole the pattern exists to prevent.
Fault<T> events and the *_error queue are different destinations; consuming faults is not the same as draining the error queue, so both need an owner.
Skipped messages go to *_skipped, not *_error - a message with no matching consumer is a topology problem, not an invalid payload, and confusing the two hides misrouting.
